dictionary.Plain English: A delivery that counts towards the over. Wides and no balls do not.
dictionary.Formula: Legal balls = all deliveries - wides - no balls
dictionary.Worked Example: Josh Hazlewood bowled 1,478 deliveries, of which 1,440 were legal.

dictionary.Plain English: How fast a batter scores: runs per 100 balls faced.
dictionary.Formula: SR = runs / balls faced x 100
dictionary.Worked Example: Heinrich Klaasen: 2,356 runs / 1,412 balls x 100 = 166.9.

dictionary.Plain English: Runs scored for each time the batter is out.
dictionary.Formula: Average = runs / dismissals
dictionary.Worked Example: Heinrich Klaasen: 2,356 / 58 = 40.6.

dictionary.Plain English: Runs a bowler gives away per over.
dictionary.Formula: Economy = runs conceded / legal balls x 6
dictionary.Worked Example: Josh Hazlewood: 1,979 / 1,440 x 6 = 8.24.

dictionary.Plain English: A legal ball with no run scored.
dictionary.Formula: Dot % = dot balls / legal balls x 100
dictionary.Worked Example: IPL powerplays have about 43% dot balls.

dictionary.Plain English: Powerplay is overs 1 to 6, middle overs are 7 to 16, and the death is 17 to 20.
dictionary.Formula: Grouped by over number
dictionary.Worked Example: This report splits the middle into overs 7-11 and 12-16.

dictionary.Plain English: Runs scored minus what losing a wicket costs the team.
dictionary.Formula: Ball value = runs - wicket cost
dictionary.Worked Example: A six with no wicket has a ball value of 6.

dictionary.Plain English: The runs the team is expected to lose because that wicket fell, given the balls left.
dictionary.Formula: Expected runs now - expected runs with one more wicket down
dictionary.Worked Example: Early wickets cost more than wickets in the last over.

dictionary.Plain English: What an average player gets from a ball in the same situation.
dictionary.Formula: Average ball value for the same competition, innings, phase, wickets and pressure state
dictionary.Worked Example: A last-over ball has a higher expected value than a powerplay ball.

dictionary.Plain English: How much better than average this ball was. Positive is always good.
dictionary.Formula: Batter: value - expected. Bowler: expected - value. Reported per 100 balls
dictionary.Worked Example: Heinrich Klaasen: +50.9 per 100 pressure balls before adjustment.

dictionary.Plain English: A player's normal level, measured on Ordinary balls.
dictionary.Formula: Ordinary value x balls / (balls + prior)

dictionary.Plain English: How far the player beats the level their own usual form predicts.
dictionary.Formula: Uplift = adjusted pressure value - predicted value
dictionary.Worked Example: Heinrich Klaasen: 23.18 - 11.57 = +11.62.

dictionary.Plain English: Win probability the player added per 100 pressure balls.
dictionary.Formula: Sum of win probability changes / pressure balls x 100
dictionary.Worked Example: Adjusted for sample size in the same way as value.

dictionary.Plain English: How often a player beats the expected value in a pressure innings or spell.
dictionary.Formula: (innings beaten + 10 x pool average) / (innings + 10)
dictionary.Worked Example: Heinrich Klaasen beat it in 22 of 27 pressure innings, adjusted to 75.4%.

dictionary.Plain English: The chance, from 0 to 100%, that the batting side wins from this exact situation.
dictionary.Formula: Logistic model using target, runs needed, balls left, wickets in hand and scoring era
dictionary.Worked Example: In the worked example, Rajasthan Royals had a 48.7% chance.

dictionary.Plain English: How much the next ball can change the win probability. High leverage means the ball matters.
dictionary.Formula: Square root of: sum of chance x (win after - average win after) squared
dictionary.Worked Example: In the worked example, one ball could move the result by about 12.08 points.

dictionary.Plain English: How evenly poised the match is. 100 is a coin toss and 0 is decided.
dictionary.Formula: Closeness = 100 x (1 - |2 x win probability - 1|)
dictionary.Worked Example: At 48.7% win probability, closeness is 97.3.

dictionary.Plain English: How much of the innings has gone. Late mistakes leave less time to recover.
dictionary.Formula: Stage = 100 x (1 - balls left / total balls)
dictionary.Worked Example: With 7 balls left of 120, stage is 94.2.

dictionary.Plain English: Recent trouble. For batters it counts recent wickets and dots. For bowlers it counts runs leaked.
dictionary.Formula: Batter: 60 x min(wickets in 18 balls / 2, 1) + 40 x min(dots in 12 balls / 8, 1)
dictionary.Worked Example: In the worked example, stress is 80.0.

dictionary.Plain English: One score out of about 100 that says how tense this ball is.
dictionary.Formula: 0.40 x leverage % + 0.20 x closeness + 0.25 x stage + 0.15 x stress + 5 if a knockout
dictionary.Worked Example: Worked example: 95.0, which is Extreme.

dictionary.Plain English: Ordinary, High or Extreme. Decided matches are always Ordinary.
dictionary.Formula: Batting view: High from 59.4, Extreme from 69.7
dictionary.Worked Example: The top 10% of live balls are Extreme and the next 20% are High.

dictionary.Plain English: We re-run the ranking 500 times on resampled matches to see how much a rank moves.
dictionary.Formula: 5th to 95th percentile of the 500 simulated ranks
dictionary.Worked Example: A range of 1 to 9 is firm. A range of 3 to 53 is uncertain.

dictionary.Plain English: Split matches into two random halves and check whether the two rankings agree.
dictionary.Formula: Rank correlation corrected to the full sample size
dictionary.Worked Example: 0 means no agreement and 1 means perfect agreement.

dictionary.Plain English: A small sample can be luck. Trust is the share of a player's own record we accept.
dictionary.Formula: Trust = balls / (balls + prior strength)

dictionary.Plain English: The player's record blended with the level their ordinary form predicts.
dictionary.Formula: Predicted + (raw - predicted) x trust

dictionary.Plain English: The final score. 50 is an average eligible player.
dictionary.Formula: 50 + 13 x weighted score / spread of weighted scores
dictionary.Worked Example: Weights: value 40%, uplift 20%, win impact 15%, consistency 15%, extreme 10%.

dictionary.Plain English: Blends pressure with quality, form, trajectory, versatility and availability.
dictionary.Formula: 45% pressure + 20% quality + 15% form + 5% trajectory + 10% versatility + 5% availability
dictionary.Worked Example: Each part is a percentile within batters or bowlers.

dictionary.Plain English: How well a player's role matches RR's measured weak spots.
dictionary.Formula: Based on RR's pressure gap in the phases that role plays
dictionary.Worked Example: Death bowling is the largest gap.

dictionary.Plain English: The number used to order the RR investment list.
dictionary.Formula: 85% Potential Score + 15% RR Fit
dictionary.Worked Example: Squad limits then apply: at most 4 overseas and 3 per role.
